text:
maya: Quick pass on the dashboard chart — proposing a compact visual hierarchy for the model performance panel. Main goals: reduce vertical clutter, make units explicit, and avoid misleading smoothing on latency spikes.

samir: Can you sketch the changes? Not sure what you mean by compact hierarchy. :thinking_face:

maya: Short sketch: 1) axis labels show units on one line: `Latency (ms)` or `Tokens / s` — avoid parentheses wrapping multiple lines; 2) legend becomes collapsible with a small summary line (e.g., `3 series • 2 hidden`) to save vertical space; 3) default smoothing OFF for latency graphs (we still offer a 5s smooth toggle).

oliver: +1 on smoothing default. Spikes matter for SLOs. If we smooth by default people will miss regressions. Could we make the smoothing control more discoverable (inline toggle next to the time range)?

jess: UX nit on units — we have multiple places using `per 1k tokens` vs `per 1000 tokens`. Let's standardize to `per 1k tokens` in UI copy. Also: tooltips should show exact unit conversion, e.g., `avg_latency: 12.3 ms (per request)`

maya: Good call. Standardize copy to `per 1k tokens`. For the axis truncation, I propose truncating long metric names and exposing full name on hover. Example abbreviated axis: `Throughput (tokens/s)` -> show full on tooltip.

design-bot: Snapshot attached: /images/snap-1827569102-compact-hierarchy.png (preview). Reaction counts: :eyes: x3

pm-lee: Accessibility: ensure color palette meets 4.5:1 contrast for foreground text on legend chips and that we have a colorblind-safe set for series. Also keyboard focus for collapsed legend items (ability to expand via keyboard).

samir: For outliers handling — current options are: cap (clamp to 99th percentile), hide (exclude outliers), and show (raw). I vote for cap as default but with an explicit banner: `Outliers capped to 99th percentile. View raw data -> toggle`. Banner should link to docs.

oliver: I worry capping hides root cause sometimes. Can we show a faint marker above the cap to indicate number of capped points? e.g., small chevron with count. That keeps the chart readable but signals the truncation.

maya: Love the chevron idea. Mockup note: chevron shows `+7` meaning 7 points above cap. Hover shows a mini-list with timestamps. If user clicks it, opens the raw-view modal.

jess: Copy tweak suggestion for the modal CTA: use `Inspect raw outliers` instead of `Show raw` — more explicit.

samir: Minor perf thought — legend collapse/expand should be client-side only, no extra network calls. State persisted in local storage per-user.

maya: Action items: 1) design to build compact mock + chevron for capped outliers (maya,jess) 2) dev to make smoothing default off and add inline toggle (samir,oliver) 3) copy guide: standardize unit strings to `per 1k tokens` and update tooltips/docs (jess) 4) accessibility pass on palette & keyboard (pm-lee). I'll upload updated mock by EOD.

samir: Sounds good. One more: legend ordering — prefer ordering by max value in viewport (most important first) rather than alphabetic. That will bring the heavy hitters up. Agree?

jess: Agree, but keep persistent user override (pin order).

maya: OK final note — include a short in-UI hint the first time a user encounters the new legend behavior: `Legend sorted by impact in current view — pin to keep custom order` with an inline `Got it` dismiss.

oliver: :thumbsup:

design-bot: New mock uploaded: /images/snap-1827569650-compact-hierarchy-v2.png

maya: Thanks all — I'll update the Figma and link here when ready.
